subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the NET yield of ATP from one molecule of glucose during glycolysis alone?
options: 4 ATP
38 ATP
2 ATP
1 ATP
questions.explain: Four ATP are produced but two are invested in the early phosphorylation steps, giving a net gain of two ATP.

questions.q: As an organism increases in size, why does it require a specialised exchange surface?
options: Larger cells respire anaerobically and need no oxygen
Its surface-area-to-volume ratio increases, slowing diffusion
Its surface-area-to-volume ratio decreases, so diffusion across the body surface cannot meet metabolic demand
Volume increases more slowly than surface area
questions.explain: As size increases, volume rises faster than surface area, so the SA:V ratio falls and the body surface alone cannot supply the cells.

questions.q: A respiratory substrate gives a respiratory quotient (RQ) of about 0.7. Which substrate is most likely being respired?
options: Protein
Ethanol
Carbohydrate
Lipid
questions.explain: Lipids are highly reduced and require more oxygen relative to CO2 produced, giving an RQ around 0.7.

questions.q: In a fish gill, the counter-current flow of water and blood is efficient because:
options: A diffusion gradient for oxygen is maintained across the entire length of the lamella
It allows carbon dioxide to be reabsorbed into the blood
Blood and water flow in the same direction, equalising oxygen quickly
Water flows faster than blood, reversing the gradient
questions.explain: Counter-current flow keeps the oxygen concentration of water higher than that of blood along the whole gill lamella, maintaining a diffusion gradient throughout.

questions.q: The role of calcium ions in muscle contraction is to:
options: Bind to troponin, moving tropomyosin to expose the myosin-binding sites on actin
Break the cross-bridges between actin and myosin
Resynthesise ATP from ADP
Provide the energy for the power stroke
questions.explain: Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum binds troponin, shifting tropomyosin to uncover actin binding sites so cross-bridges can form.

questions.q: Compared with elastic recoil in expiration, why are the walls of arteries elastic?
options: To allow active contraction that pumps blood
To enable exchange of materials with tissues
To stretch under high pressure and recoil, smoothing out pressure surges and maintaining flow
To slow blood flow for absorption
questions.explain: Elastic tissue in artery walls stretches during systole and recoils during diastole, evening out pulsatile pressure and sustaining blood flow.

questions.q: During ventricular systole, the atrioventricular valves close because:
options: Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
The ventricles are relaxing and filling
The semilunar valves are open
Ventricular pressure exceeds atrial pressure
questions.explain: As the ventricles contract their pressure rises above that of the atria, forcing the AV valves shut to prevent backflow.

questions.q: During inspiration in a mammal, the pressure in the thorax falls because:
options: The diaphragm relaxes and domes upward
Surfactant reduces the surface tension of the alveoli
The external intercostal muscles relax
The volume of the thoracic cavity increases as the diaphragm flattens and the ribs move up and out
questions.explain: Contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostals increases thoracic volume, lowering pressure below atmospheric so air flows in.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of stages in aerobic respiration?
options: Glycolysis then Krebs cycle then link reaction then oxidative phosphorylation
Krebs cycle then glycolysis then oxidative phosphorylation then link reaction
Glycolysis then link reaction then Krebs cycle then oxidative phosphorylation
Link reaction then glycolysis then Krebs cycle then oxidative phosphorylation
questions.explain: Glucose is split in glycolysis, pyruvate enters the link reaction, then the Krebs cycle, then oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.q: What is the approximate respiratory quotient (RQ) for the complete aerobic respiration of a carbohydrate such as glucose?
questions.explain: For glucose the volumes of CO2 produced and O2 consumed are equal, giving an RQ of 1.0.

questions.q: When blood glucose rises after a meal, insulin lowers it by:
options: Increasing the uptake of glucose by cells and promoting glycogenesis
Inhibiting respiration in muscle cells
Stimulating glycogenolysis in the liver
Converting amino acids and glycerol into glucose
questions.explain: Insulin raises glucose uptake (via more GLUT4 channels) and promotes glycogenesis, converting glucose to glycogen for storage.

questions.q: The semilunar (aortic and pulmonary) valves open when:
options: Ventricular pressure exceeds the pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery
The AV valves are also open
Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
The ventricles relax during diastole
questions.explain: Once ventricular pressure rises above arterial pressure the semilunar valves open and blood is ejected.
